title: Membership for a prescribed input-certificate split
statement: Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet, let $C,c$ be natural numbers, and let $x,u$ be finite binary words satisfying $|u|=C(|x|+1)^c$. Then the concatenation $xu$ belongs to the choice-word verifier language of $N$ with parameters $C,c$ if and only if the run of $N$ on input $x$ under $u$ is halted with output exactly the one-bit word $[1]$.
hypotheses_covered: A finite nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ over the binary alphabet
replaced: Let $N$ be a nondeterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet, let $C, c$ be natural numbers, and let $x$ and $u$ be binary strings with $|u| = C\,(|x|+1)^c$. Then the concatenation $x\,u$ belongs to the choice-word verifier language of $N$ with parameters $C, c$ if and only if the run of $N$ on input $x$ under choice word $u$ has halted with output exactly the one-bit string $1$.
